(2005). "Kyūshū" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|''Japan Encyclopedia'', p. 588|page=588}} In the past, it has been known as {{nihongo3|"Nine Countries"|九国|Kyūkoku}}, {{nihongo3|"West of the Pacified Area"|鎮西|Chinzei}} and {{nihongo3|"Island of Tsukushi"|{{lang|ja|筑紫島}}|Tsukushi-no-shima}}. The historical regional name {{nihongo|[[:en:Saikaidō|Saikaidō]]|{{lang|ja|西海道}}||{{lit}} West Sea [[:en:Circuit (country subdivision)|Circuit]]}} referred to Kyushu and its surrounding islands. Kyushu has a land area of {{convert|36782|km2|sqmi}} and a population of 14,311,224 in 2018. In the 8th-century [[:en:Taihō Code|Taihō Code]] reforms, [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] was established as a special administrative term for the region.Nussbaum, "Dazaifu" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|p. 150|page=150}}; [http://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4850.html Dazaifu] ==Geography== [[File:Kyushu-Japan-ISS-Space.png|thumb|250px|Kyushu from the [[:en:International Space Station|International Space Station]]]] [[File:Geofeatures_map_of_Kyushu_Japan_ja.svg|thumb|315x315px|Geofeatures map of Kyushu]] The island is mountainous, and Japan's most active volcano, [[:en:Mount Aso|Mount Aso]] at {{convert|1591|m}}, is on Kyushu. There are many other signs of tectonic activity, including numerous areas of [[:en:Hot spring|Hot spring]]s. The most famous of these are in [[:en:Beppu, Ōita|Beppu]], on the east shore, and around Mt. Aso in central Kyushu. The island is separated from [[Honshu]] by the [[:en:Kanmon Straits|Kanmon Straits]]. Being the nearest island to the [[:en:Asia|Asian continent]],Nussbaum, Louis-Frédéric and Käthe Roth (2005). [https://books.google.com/books?id=p2QnPijAEmEC ''Japan Encyclopedia'']. Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-674-01753-5}}. {{OCLC|58053128}}. historically it is the gateway to Japan.{{Cite book |title=Kyushu, gateway to Japan : a concise history |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=157 |oclc=754792858}} The total area is {{convert|36,782.37|km²|sqmi|abbr=on}} which makes it the 37th [[:en:en:List of islands by area|largest island]] in the world.{{Cite web |date=2016-10-01 |url=http://www.gsi.go.jp/KOKUJYOHO/MENCHO/201610/f3_shima.pdf |title=平成28th year 全国都道府県市区町村別面積調 島面積 |publisher=[[国土地理院]] |accessdate=2017-02-27}} It's slightly larger than [[:en:Geography of Taiwan|Taiwan]] island {{convert|35,808|km2|sqmi|abbr=on}}.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thoughtco.com/islands-of-japan-1435071|title=Discover the Geography of the 4 Main Islands of Japan |work=ThoughtCo |access-date=2018-09-26}} The highest elevation is {{convert|1791|m|0|abbr=off|comma=5|sp=us}} on [[Mount Kujū]].{{cite web |url=http://www.peaklist.org/WWlists/ultras/japan.html |title=Japan Ultra-Prominences |publisher=Peaklist.org |accessdate=2015-01-01}} The name ''Kyūshū'' comes from the nine ancient provinces of [[:en:Saikaidō|Saikaidō]] situated on the island: [[:en:Chikuzen Province|Chikuzen]], [[:en:Chikugo Province|Chikugo]], [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen]], [[:en:Higo Province|Higo]], [[:en:Buzen Province|Buzen]], [[:en:Bungo Province|Bungo]], [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga]], [[:en:Ōsumi Province|Osumi]], and [[:en:Satsuma Province|Satsuma]].{{Cite book|title=Kyushu, Gateway to Japan: A Concise History |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=3 |oclc=754792858}} Today's {{nihongo|Kyushu Region|{{lang|ja|九州地方}}|Kyūshū-chihō}} is a politically defined region that consists of the seven [[:en:Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s on the island of Kyushu (which also includes the former [[:en:Tsushima Province|Tsushima]] and [[:en:Iki Province|Iki]] as part of Nagasaki), plus [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]] to the south: * [[:en:Northern Kyushu|Northern Kyushu]] ** [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] ** [[:en:Kumamoto Prefecture|Kumamoto Prefecture]] ** [[:en:Nagasaki Prefecture|Nagasaki Prefecture]] ** [[:en:Ōita Prefecture|Ōita Prefecture]] ** [[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] * [[:en:Southern Kyushu|Southern Kyushu]] ** [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]] ** [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] *[[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] ** [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]] ==Population== Kyushu has 10.3{{nbsp}}percent of the population of Japan.{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=90C4DgAAQBAJ&pg=PA16| page=16| title=The Philippine Archipelago |first=Yves |last=Boquet |publisher=Springer |year= 2017|isbn= 9783319519265}} Most of Kyushu's population is concentrated along the northwest, in the cities of [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka]] and [[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]], with population corridors stretching southwest into [[:en:Sasebo|Sasebo]] and [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki]] and south into [[:en:Kumamoto|Kumamoto]] and [[:en:Kagoshima|Kagoshima]]. Except for [[:en:Ōita (city)|Oita]] and [[:en:Miyazaki (city)|Miyazaki]], the eastern seaboard shows a general [[:en:Demographics of Japan|decline in population]]. Politically, Kyushu is described as a stronghold of the [[:en:Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]].{{cite news|title=Japanese voters want a plan to handle a declining population|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21730003-election-campaign-disappointing-them-japanese-voters-want-plan-handle-declining|newspaper=[[:en:The Economist|The Economist]]|date=5 October 2017}} Per Japanese census data,{{Cite web|url=https://www.citypopulation.de/en/japan/cities/fukuoka/|title=Fukuoka (Japan): Prefecture, Major Cities & Towns - Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |website=www.citypopulation.de}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.demographia.com/db-japanpref.htm|title=Japan Prefectures Population from 1920 and Area |website=www.demographia.com}} the Kyushu region's population with [[:en:Ryukyu Islands|Ryukyu Islands]] ([[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] and [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]] Prefectures) has experienced a large population decline since around 2000. However, the population decline in total is mild because of the relatively high birth rate of [[:en:Ryukyuans|Ryukyuans]] both within the Ryukyuan lands ([[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] and [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima]]) and throughout the Kyushu region. In addition, the other prefectures in Kyushu also have exceptionally high [[Total fertility rate#Japan|TFR]]s compared to the rest of Japan.[https://www8.cao.go.jp/shoushi/shoushika/research/cyousa23/kankyo/pdf/5.pdf 「都市と地方における子育て環境の違いから得られた知見」]{{Cite web|url=https://www.mhlw.go.jp/toukei/saikin/hw/jinkou/geppo/nengai20/dl/h9.pdf|title=令和２年(2020)人口動態統計月報年計（概数）の概況}} The Ryukyuans are an [[:en:Indigenous peoples|indigenous]] minority group in Japan. {| |+'''Historical populations''' |valign="top"|'''Including [[:en:Ryukyu Islands|Ryukyu Islands]]''' {{Historical populations | 1873 | 5,163,730 | 1920 | 8,730,000 | 1930 | 9,647,000 | 1940 | 10,511,000 | 1950 | 13,011,000 | 1960 | 13,787,000 | 1970 | 13,016,000 | 1980 | 14,073,000 | 1990 | 14,518,000 | 2000 | 14,763,781 | 2010 | 14,596,783 | 2018 | 14,311,224 |align = none | footnote = Includes Okinawa and Kagoshima prefecture populations. }} |'''Excluding Ryukyu Islands''' {{Historical populations | 1873 | 4,776,363 | 1920 | 6,742,000 | 1930 | 7,512,000 | 1940 | 8,347,000 | 1950 | 10,292,000 | 1960 | 10,941,000 | 1970 | 10,342,000 | 1980 | 11,181,000 | 1990 | 11,498,000 | 2000 | 11,659,367 | 2010 | 11,497,723 | 2018 | 11,249,154 |align = none | footnote = In 1873, [[:en:Ōsumi Province|Ōsumi Province]] represents portion of Kagoshima with Ryukyu islands }} |} ===Designated cities=== * [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka]] (population: 1,588,924) * [[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]] (population: 940,978) * [[:en:Kumamoto|Kumamoto]] (population: 738,907) ===Core cities=== * [[:en:Kagoshima|Kagoshima]] * [[:en:Ōita (city)|Ōita]] * [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki]] * [[:en:Miyazaki (city)|Miyazaki]] * [[:en:Naha|Naha]] * [[:en:Kurume|Kurume]] * [[:en:Sasebo|Sasebo]] * [[:en:Saga (city)|Saga]] ==Environment and agriculture== Parts of Kyushu have a [[:en:Subtropical climate|Subtropical climate]], particularly [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] and [[:en:Kagoshima Prefecture|Kagoshima Prefecture]]. Major agricultural products are [[:en:Rice|Rice]], [[:en:Tea|Tea]], [[:en:Tobacco|Tobacco]], [[:en:Sweet potato|Sweet potato]]es, and [[:en:Soy|Soy]]; also, [[:en:Silk|Silk]] is widely produced. Besides the [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] area of the south, there are significant mud [[:en:Hot spring|Hot spring]] in the northern part of the island, around [[:en:Beppu|Beppu]]. The springs are the site of occurrence of certain [[:en:Extremophile|Extremophile]] [[:en:Microorganism|Microorganism]]s, which are capable of surviving in extremely hot environments.C. Michael Hogan. 2010. [http://www.eoearth.org/article/Extremophile?topic=49540 ''Extremophile'']. eds. E. Monosson and C. Cleveland. Encyclopedia of Earth. National Council for Science and the Environment, Washington DC There are two World Natural Heritage sites in Kyushu: [[:en:Yakushima|Yakushima]] (registered in 1993) and [[:en:Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island]] (registered in 2021).{{Cite web|title=日本の世界遺産一覧 |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/|website=文化庁|language=ja| access-date=2023-05-22}} ==Economy == {{main|Economy of Japan}} [[Image:M-V with ASTRO-E2 on launch pad.jpeg|thumb|M-V rocket launch rehearsal at USC]] Kyushu's economy accounts for about 10% of Japan's total, and with a GDP equivalent to that of Iran, the 26th largest country in the world, it is the fourth largest economic zone after the three major metropolitan areas of [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], [[:en:Osaka|Osaka]], and [[:en:Nagoya|Nagoya]].{{Cite web|title=potential of Kyushu |url=https://www.fukuoka-fg.com/vision/03.html|website=Fukuoka financial group|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-16}} Kyushu's economy has a well-balanced industrial structure, ranging from primary industries such as agriculture, to secondary industries such as manufacturing, and tertiary industries such as retail, services, and tourism. Agricultural output in the region amounts to 1.8 trillion yen (20% share of the national total), and the region is a major domestic production center for the [[:en:Automobile|Automobile]] and [[:en:Semiconductor|Semiconductor]] industries. Kyushu also has a thriving healthcare industry, including medical and nursing care, and numerous research and manufacturing facilities in the fields of [[:en:Hydrogen|Hydrogen]], [[:en:Solar power|Solar power]], and other renewable energies. Furthermore, [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], [[:en:Kitakyushu City|Kitakyushu City]] and [[:en:Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa Prefecture]] have been designated as [[National Strategic Special Zones]], which are expected to have an economic ripple effect on the entire Kyushu region through the creation of innovation in industry and the promotion of new entrepreneurship and start-ups. Kyushu is a region with strong economic ties to Asia. For example, Asia accounted for 420 (77.9%) of the 539 overseas expansion cases of Kyushu-Yamaguchi companies from 2010 to 2019, and Asia accounted for 61.1% of Kyushu-Yamaguchi's total exports in 2019, 7.4 percentage points higher than the nation as a whole. As the logistics node between Japan and Asia, the ports of Hakata and Kitakyushu handle a large number of international containers. In addition, the number of cruise ship calls in 2019 was 772, with Kyushu accounting for 26.9% of the nation's total.{{Cite web|title=はじめての九州経済 |url=https://www.kerc.or.jp/economy/gaikan/|website=Kyushu economic research center|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-22}} Kyushu is noted for various types of [[:en:Porcelain|Porcelain]], including Arita, Imari, Satsuma, and Karatsu. [[:en:Heavy industry|Heavy industry]] is concentrated in the north around Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, Nagasaki, and Oita and includes chemicals, automobiles, semiconductors, metal processing, shipbuilding, etc.{{Cite web|title=JAPAN PRODUCTS: Business Directory of Japanese Companies.|url=http://japan-product.com/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-28}} The island of [[:en:Tanegashima|Tanegashima]] hosts the [[:en:Tanegashima Space Center|Tanegashima Space Center]], which is the largest rocket-launch complex in Japan. ==Transportation== Kyushu is linked to the larger island of [[Honshu]] by the [[:en:Kanmon Railway Tunnel|Kanmon Railway Tunnel]],{{Cite web|title=Kanmon Tunnel {{!}} Description, History, Construction, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kanmon-Tunnel|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}} which carries the non-[[:en:Shinkansen|Shinkansen]] trains of the [[:en:Kyushu Railway Company|Kyushu Railway Company]], and the newer [[:en:Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel]] carrying the [[:en:San'yō Shinkansen|San'yō Shinkansen]]. Railways on the island are operated by the Kyushu Railway Company and [[:en:West Japan Railway Company|West Japan Railway Company]], as well as a variety of smaller companies such as [[:en:Amagi Railway Amagi Line|Amagi Railway]]{{Cite web|title=Railways in Kyushu|url=https://www.sinfin.net/railways/world/japan/kyushu.html|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.sinfin.net}} and [[:en:Nishi-Nippon Railroad|Nishitetsu Railway]].{{Cite web|title=Railways in Northern Kyushu|url=http://www.japaneserailwaysociety.com/jrs/members/oliver/kyushu/kyushu.htm|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.japaneserailwaysociety.com}} [[:en:Kyushu Shinkansen|Kyushu Shinkansen]] trains operate between major cities on the island,{{Cite web|title=Getting Around {{!}} Kyushu Tourism Promotion Organization|url=https://www.visit-kyushu.com/en/plan-your-trip/getting-around/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.visit-kyushu.com|language=en}} such as [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka]] and [[:en:Kagoshima|Kagoshima]],{{Cite web|title=Kyushu Shinkansen|url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=[[Japan Visitor]] |archive-date=2021-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020112050/https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen}} with an additional route between {{STN|Takeo-Onsen}} and [[:en:Nagasaki|Nagasaki]] which is in operation since September 2022.{{Cite web|date=2020-07-10|title=Fukuoka to Nagasaki: How to go from Fukuoka to Nagasaki? {{!}} Japan-Rail-Pass|url=https://www.japan-rail-pass.com/node/4326|access-date=2022-04-21|website=Japan Rail Pass {{!}} Japan Rail Pass |language=en}} Kyushu is also known for its scenic train services, such as the Limited Express Yufuin no Mori and Limited Express Kawasemi Yamasemi. The [[:en:Kanmon Bridge|Kanmon Bridge]] and [[:en:Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel]] also connect the island with Honshu, allowing for vehicular transport between the two.{{Cite web|last=MATCHA |title=Walk From Honshu To Kyushu! 4 Ways To Cross Between The Two Islands|url=https://matcha-jp.com/en/1737|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MATCHA - JAPAN TRAVEL WEB MAGAZINE |language=en}} The [[:en:Kyushu Expressway|Kyushu Expressway]] spans the length of the island, linking the [[:en:Higashikyushu Expressway|Higashikyushu Expressway]] and Ibusuki Skyline, connecting major cities such as [[:en:Fukuoka|Fukuoka]] and [[:en:Kumamoto|Kumamoto]] along the way.{{Cite web |title=Kyushu Expy · Japan |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Kyushu+Expy,+Japan/@32.7319959,130.7735981,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x3540f3427949e6d9:0x60891c7c25263c3!8m2!3d32.7319914!4d130.7757868 |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=Kyushu Expy · Japan |language=en}} There are also many quiet country roads, including popular tourist routes such as the [[:en:Nichinan, Miyazaki|Nichinan]] coast road and the Aso Panorama Line in [[:en:Kumamoto Prefecture|Kumamoto Prefecture]]. Bus services are available and cover 2,400 routes within Kyushu's cities, connecting many other destinations. Several passenger and car ferry services connect both northern and southern Kyushu with main port cities on the main island of Honshu (Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo) and [[Shikoku]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2355.html|title = Domestic Ferries| date=May 2022 }} ==Education== [[File:Kyushumap-en.png|320px|thumb|Map of Kyushu region with prefectures]] [[File:JMSDF major (2005). "Kyūshū" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|''Japan Encyclopedia'', p. 588|page=588}} In the past, it has been known as {{nihongo3|"Nine Countries"|九国|Kyūkoku}}, {{nihongo3|"West of the Pacified Area"|鎮西|Chinzei}} and {{nihongo3|"Island of Tsukushi"|{{lang|ja|筑紫島}}|Tsukushi-no-shima}}. The historical regional name {{nihongo|{{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}}|{{lang|ja|西海道}}||{{lit}} West Sea [[:en:Circuit (country subdivision)|Circuit]]}} referred to Kyushu and its surrounding islands. Kyushu has a land area of {{convert|36782|km2|sqmi}} and a population of 14,311,224 in 2018. In the 8th-century {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|WD=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} reforms, {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} was established as a special administrative term for the region.Nussbaum, "Dazaifu" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|p. 150|page=150}}; [http://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4850.html Dazaifu] ==Geography== [[File:Kyushu-Japan-ISS-Space.png|thumb|250px|Kyushu from the {{ill|International Space Station|en|International Space Station|WD=Q25271|lt=International Space Station}}]] [[File:Geofeatures_map_of_Kyushu_Japan_ja.svg|thumb|315x315px|Geofeatures map of Kyushu]] The island is mountainous, and Japan's most active volcano, {{ill|Mount Aso|en|Mount Aso|WD=Q733710|lt=Mount Aso}} at {{convert|1591|m}}, is on Kyushu. There are many other signs of tectonic activity, including numerous areas of {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}}s. The most famous of these are in [[:en:Beppu, Ōita|Beppu]], on the east shore, and around Mt. Aso in central Kyushu. The island is separated from [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Straits|en|Kanmon Straits|WD=Q494894|lt=Kanmon Straits}}. Being the nearest island to the {{ill|Asia|en|Asia|WD=Q48|lt=Asian continent}},Nussbaum, Louis-Frédéric and Käthe Roth (2005). [https://books.google.com/books?id=p2QnPijAEmEC ''Japan Encyclopedia'']. Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-674-01753-5}}. {{OCLC|58053128}}. historically it is the gateway to Japan.{{Cite book |title=Kyushu, gateway to Japan : a concise history |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=157 |oclc=754792858}} The total area is {{convert|36,782.37|km²|sqmi|abbr=on}} which makes it the 37th {{ill|en:List of islands by area|en|en:List of islands by area|WD=Q104176|lt=largest island}} in the world.{{Cite web |date=2016-10-01 |url=http://www.gsi.go.jp/KOKUJYOHO/MENCHO/201610/f3_shima.pdf Politically, Kyushu is described as a stronghold of the {{ill|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|en|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|WD=Q232595|lt=Liberal Democratic Party}}.{{cite news|title=Japanese voters want a plan to handle a declining population|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21730003-election-campaign-disappointing-them-japanese-voters-want-plan-handle-declining|newspaper={{ill|The Economist|en|The Economist|WD=Q180089|lt=The Economist}}|date=5 October 2017}} Per Japanese census data,{{Cite web|url=https://www.citypopulation.de/en/japan/cities/fukuoka/|title=Fukuoka (Japan): Prefecture, Major Cities & Towns - Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |website=www.citypopulation.de}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.demographia.com/db-japanpref.htm|title=Japan Prefectures Population from 1920 and Area |website=www.demographia.com}} the Kyushu region's population with {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|en|Ryukyu Islands|WD=Q6897416|lt=Ryukyu Islands}} ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}} Prefectures) has experienced a large population decline since around 2000. However, the population decline in total is mild because of the relatively high birth rate of {{ill|Ryukyuans|en|Ryukyuans|WD=Q1208167|lt=Ryukyuans}} both within the Ryukyuan lands ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}}) and throughout the Kyushu region. have a [[:en:Subtropical climate|Subtropical climate]], particularly {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture}}. Major agricultural products are {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}}, {{ill|Tea|en|Tea|WD=Q6097|lt=Tea}}, {{ill|Tobacco|en|Tobacco|WD=Q1566|lt=Tobacco}}, {{ill|Sweet potato|en|Sweet potato|WD=Q37937|lt=Sweet potato}}es, and [[:en:Soy|Soy]]; also, {{ill|Silk|en|Silk|WD=Q37681|lt=Silk}} is widely produced. Besides the [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] area of the south, there are significant mud {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}} in the northern part of the island, around {{ill|Beppu|en|Beppu|WD=Q273880|lt=Beppu}}. The springs are the site of occurrence of certain {{ill|Extremophile|en|Extremophile|WD=Q206912|lt=Extremophile}} {{ill|Microorganism|en|Microorganism|WD=Q39833|lt=Microorganism}}s, which are capable of surviving in extremely hot environments.C. Michael Hogan. 2010. [http://www.eoearth.org/article/Extremophile?topic=49540 ''Extremophile'']. eds. E. Monosson and C. Cleveland. Encyclopedia of Earth. National Council for Science and the Environment, Washington DC There are two World Natural Heritage sites in Kyushu: {{ill|Yakushima|en|Yakushima|WD=Q242176|lt=Yakushima}} (registered in 1993) and {{ill|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|en|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|WD=Q11444847|lt=Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island}} (registered in 2021).{{Cite web|title=日本の世界遺産一覧 |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/|website=文化庁|language=ja| access-date=2023-05-22}} ==Economy == {{main|Economy of Japan}} [[Image:M-V with ASTRO-E2 on launch pad.jpeg|thumb|M-V rocket launch rehearsal at USC]] Kyushu's economy accounts for about 10% of Japan's total, and with a GDP equivalent to that of Iran, the 26th largest country in the world, it is the fourth largest economic zone after the three major metropolitan areas of {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}, and {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|WD=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}}.{{Cite web|title=potential of Kyushu |url=https://www.fukuoka-fg.com/vision/03.html|website=Fukuoka financial group|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-16}} Kyushu's economy has a well-balanced industrial structure, ranging from primary industries such as agriculture, to secondary industries such as manufacturing, and tertiary industries such as retail, services, and tourism. Agricultural output in the region amounts to 1.8 trillion yen (20% share of the national total), and the region is a major domestic production center for the [[:en:Automobile|Automobile]] and {{ill|Semiconductor|en|Semiconductor|WD=Q11456|lt=Semiconductor}} industries. Kyushu also has a thriving healthcare industry, including medical and nursing care, and numerous research and manufacturing facilities in the fields of {{ill|Hydrogen|en|Hydrogen|WD=Q556|lt=Hydrogen}}, {{ill|Solar power|en|Solar power|WD=Q1483757|lt=Solar power}}, and other renewable energies. Furthermore, [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], [[:en:Kitakyushu City|Kitakyushu City]] and {{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa Prefecture}} have been designated as [[National Strategic Special Zones]], which are expected to have an economic ripple effect on the entire Kyushu region through the creation of innovation in industry and the promotion of new entrepreneurship and start-ups. Kyushu is a region with strong economic ties to Asia. For example, Asia accounted for 420 (77.9%) of the 539 overseas expansion cases of Kyushu-Yamaguchi companies from 2010 to 2019, and Asia accounted for 61.1% of Kyushu-Yamaguchi's total exports in 2019, 7.4 percentage points higher than the nation as a whole. As the logistics node between Japan and Asia, the ports of Hakata and Kitakyushu handle a large number of international containers. In addition, the number of cruise ship calls in 2019 was 772, with Kyushu accounting for 26.9% of the nation's total.{{Cite web|title=はじめての九州経済 |url=https://www.kerc.or.jp/economy/gaikan/|website=Kyushu economic research center|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-22}} Kyushu is noted for various types of {{ill|Porcelain|en|Porcelain|WD=Q130693|lt=Porcelain}}, including Arita, Imari, Satsuma, and Karatsu. {{ill|Heavy industry|en|Heavy industry|WD=Q622662|lt=Heavy industry}} is concentrated in the north around Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, Nagasaki, and Oita and includes chemicals, automobiles, semiconductors, metal processing, shipbuilding, etc.{{Cite web|title=JAPAN PRODUCTS: Business Directory of Japanese Companies.|url=http://japan-product.com/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-28}} The island of {{ill|Tanegashima|en|Tanegashima|WD=Q696228|lt=Tanegashima}} hosts the {{ill|Tanegashima Space Center|en|Tanegashima Space Center|WD=Q742683|lt=Tanegashima Space Center}}, which is the largest rocket-launch complex in Japan. ==Transportation== Kyushu is linked to the larger island of [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|WD=Q15972411|lt=Kanmon Railway Tunnel}},{{Cite web|title=Kanmon Tunnel {{!}} Description, History, Construction, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kanmon-Tunnel|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}} which carries the non-{{ill|Shinkansen|en|Shinkansen|WD=Q164338|lt=Shinkansen}} trains of the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}}, and the newer {{ill|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|en|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|WD=Q8016189|lt=Shin-Kanmon Tunnel}} carrying the {{ill|San'yō Shinkansen|en|San'yō Shinkansen|WD=Q615964|lt=San'yō Shinkansen}}. Railways on the island are operated by the Kyushu Railway Company and {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|WD=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}}, as well as a variety of smaller companies such as {{ill|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|en|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|WD=Q642407|lt=Amagi Railway}}{{Cite web|title=Railways in Kyushu|url=https://www.sinfin.net/railways/world/japan/kyushu.html|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.sinfin.net}} and {{ill|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|en|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|WD=Q869251|lt=Nishitetsu Railway}}.{{Cite web|title=Railways in Northern Kyushu|url=http://www.japaneserailwaysociety.com/jrs/members/oliver/kyushu/kyushu.htm|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.japaneserailwaysociety.com}} {{ill|Kyushu Shinkansen|en|Kyushu Shinkansen|WD=Q11370254|lt=Kyushu Shinkansen}} trains operate between major cities on the island,{{Cite web|title=Getting Around {{!}} Kyushu Tourism Promotion Organization|url=https://www.visit-kyushu.com/en/plan-your-trip/getting-around/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.visit-kyushu.com|language=en}} such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kagoshima|en|Kagoshima|WD=Q15674|lt=Kagoshima}},{{Cite web|title=Kyushu Shinkansen|url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=[[Japan Visitor]] |archive-date=2021-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020112050/https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen}} with an additional route between {{STN|Takeo-Onsen}} and {{ill|Nagasaki|en|Nagasaki|WD=Q38234|lt=Nagasaki}} which is in operation since September 2022.{{Cite web|date=2020-07-10|title=Fukuoka to Nagasaki: How to go from Fukuoka to Nagasaki? {{!}} Japan-Rail-Pass|url=https://www.japan-rail-pass.com/node/4326|access-date=2022-04-21|website=Japan Rail Pass {{!}} Japan Rail Pass |language=en}} Kyushu is also known for its scenic train services, such as the Limited Express Yufuin no Mori and Limited Express Kawasemi Yamasemi. The {{ill|Kanmon Bridge|en|Kanmon Bridge|WD=Q1196470|lt=Kanmon Bridge}} and {{ill|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|WD=Q15972446|lt=Kanmon Roadway Tunnel}} also connect the island with Honshu, allowing for vehicular transport between the two.{{Cite web|last=MATCHA |title=Walk From Honshu To Kyushu! 4 Ways To Cross Between The Two Islands|url=https://matcha-jp.com/en/1737|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MATCHA - JAPAN TRAVEL WEB MAGAZINE |language=en}} The {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|en|Kyushu Expressway|WD=Q1060803|lt=Kyushu Expressway}} spans the length of the island, linking the {{ill|Higashikyushu Expressway|en|Higashikyushu Expressway|WD=Q2648028|lt=Higashikyushu Expressway}} and Ibusuki Skyline, connecting major cities such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kumamoto|en|Kumamoto|WD=Q199889|lt=Kumamoto}} along the way.{{Cite web |title=Kyushu Expy · Japan |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Kyushu+Expy,+Japan/@32.7319959,130.7735981,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x3540f3427949e6d9:0x60891c7c25263c3!8m2!3d32.7319914!4d130.7757868 |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=Kyushu Expy · Japan |language=en}} There are also many quiet country roads, including popular tourist routes such as the {{ill|Nichinan, Miyazaki|en|Nichinan, Miyazaki|WD=Q860669|lt=Nichinan}} coast road and the Aso Panorama Line in {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|Kumamoto Prefecture|WD=Q130308|lt=Kumamoto Prefecture}}. Bus services are available and cover 2,400 routes within Kyushu's cities, connecting many other destinations. Several passenger and car ferry services connect both northern and southern Kyushu with main port cities on the main island of Honshu (Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo) and [[Shikoku]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2355.html|title = Domestic Ferries| date=May 2022 }} ==Education== [[File:Kyushumap-en.png|320px|thumb|Map of Kyushu region with prefectures]] [[File:JMSDF major (2005). "Kyūshū" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|''Japan Encyclopedia'', p. 588|page=588}} In the past, it has been known as {{nihongo3|"Nine Countries"|九国|Kyūkoku}}, {{nihongo3|"West of the Pacified Area"|鎮西|Chinzei}} and {{nihongo3|"Island of Tsukushi"|{{lang|ja|筑紫島}}|Tsukushi-no-shima}}. The historical regional name {{nihongo|{{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}}|{{lang|ja|西海道}}||{{lit}} West Sea [[:en:Circuit (country subdivision)|Circuit]]}} referred to Kyushu and its surrounding islands. Kyushu has a land area of {{convert|36782|km2|sqmi}} and a population of 14,311,224 in 2018. In the 8th-century {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|WD=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} reforms, {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} was established as a special administrative term for the region.Nussbaum, "Dazaifu" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|p. 150|page=150}}; [http://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4850.html Dazaifu] ==Geography== [[File:Kyushu-Japan-ISS-Space.png|thumb|250px|Kyushu from the {{ill|International Space Station|en|International Space Station|WD=Q25271|lt=International Space Station}}]] [[File:Geofeatures_map_of_Kyushu_Japan_ja.svg|thumb|315x315px|Geofeatures map of Kyushu]] The island is mountainous, and Japan's most active volcano, {{ill|Mount Aso|en|Mount Aso|WD=Q733710|lt=Mount Aso}} at {{convert|1591|m}}, is on Kyushu. There are many other signs of tectonic activity, including numerous areas of {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}}s. The most famous of these are in [[:en:Beppu, Ōita|Beppu]], on the east shore, and around Mt. Aso in central Kyushu. The island is separated from [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Straits|en|Kanmon Straits|WD=Q494894|lt=Kanmon Straits}}. Being the nearest island to the {{ill|Asia|en|Asia|WD=Q48|lt=Asian continent}},Nussbaum, Louis-Frédéric and Käthe Roth (2005). [https://books.google.com/books?id=p2QnPijAEmEC ''Japan Encyclopedia'']. Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-674-01753-5}}. {{OCLC|58053128}}. historically it is the gateway to Japan.{{Cite book |title=Kyushu, gateway to Japan : a concise history |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=157 |oclc=754792858}} The total area is {{convert|36,782.37|km²|sqmi|abbr=on}} which makes it the 37th {{ill|en:List of islands by area|en|en:List of islands by area|WD=Q104176|lt=largest island}} in the world.{{Cite web |date=2016-10-01 |url=http://www.gsi.go.jp/KOKUJYOHO/MENCHO/201610/f3_shima.pdf |title=平成28th year 全国都道府県市区町村別面積調 島面積 |publisher=[[国土地理院]] |accessdate=2017-02-27}} It's slightly larger than {{ill|Geography of Taiwan|en|Geography of Taiwan|WD=Q22528|lt=Taiwan}} island {{convert|35,808|km2|sqmi|abbr=on}}.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thoughtco.com/islands-of-japan-1435071|title=Discover the Geography of the 4 Main Islands of Japan |work=ThoughtCo |access-date=2018-09-26}} The highest elevation is {{convert|1791|m|0|abbr=off|comma=5|sp=us}} on [[Mount Kujū]].{{cite web |url=http://www.peaklist.org/WWlists/ultras/japan.html |title=Japan Ultra-Prominences |publisher=Peaklist.org |accessdate=2015-01-01}} The name ''Kyūshū'' comes from the nine ancient provinces of {{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}} situated on the island: {{ill|Chikuzen Province|en|Chikuzen Province|WD=Q1047664|lt=Chikuzen}}, {{ill|Chikugo Province|en|Chikugo Province|WD=Q864159|lt=Chikugo}}, {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Kyushu's population is concentrated along the northwest, in the cities of {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kitakyushu|en|Kitakyushu|WD=Q188806|lt=Kitakyushu}}, with population Except for {{ill|Ōita (city)|en|Ōita (city)|WD=Q199609|lt=Oita}} and {{ill|Miyazaki (city)|en|Miyazaki (city)|WD=Q204308|lt=Miyazaki}}, the eastern seaboard shows a general {{ill|Demographics of Japan|en|Demographics of Japan|WD=Q1124220|lt=decline in population}}. Politically, Kyushu is described as a stronghold of the {{ill|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|en|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|WD=Q232595|lt=Liberal Democratic Party}}.{{cite news|title=Japanese voters want a plan to handle a declining population|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21730003-election-campaign-disappointing-them-japanese-voters-want-plan-handle-declining|newspaper={{ill|The Economist|en|The Economist|WD=Q180089|lt=The Economist}}|date=5 October 2017}} Per Japanese census data,{{Cite web|url=https://www.citypopulation.de/en/japan/cities/fukuoka/|title=Fukuoka (Japan): Prefecture, Major Cities & Towns - Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |website=www.citypopulation.de}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.demographia.com/db-japanpref.htm|title=Japan Prefectures Population from 1920 and Area |website=www.demographia.com}} the Kyushu region's population with {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|en|Ryukyu Islands|WD=Q6897416|lt=Ryukyu Islands}} ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}} Prefectures) has experienced a large population decline since around 2000. However, the population decline in total is mild because of the relatively high birth rate of {{ill|Ryukyuans|en|Ryukyuans|WD=Q1208167|lt=Ryukyuans}} both within the Ryukyuan lands ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}}) and throughout the Kyushu region. In addition, the other prefectures in Kyushu also have exceptionally high [[Total fertility rate#Japan|TFR]]s compared to the rest of have a [[:en:Subtropical climate|Subtropical climate]], particularly {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture}}. Major agricultural products are {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}}, {{ill|Tea|en|Tea|WD=Q6097|lt=Tea}}, {{ill|Tobacco|en|Tobacco|WD=Q1566|lt=Tobacco}}, {{ill|Sweet potato|en|Sweet potato|WD=Q37937|lt=Sweet potato}}es, and [[:en:Soy|Soy]]; also, {{ill|Silk|en|Silk|WD=Q37681|lt=Silk}} is widely produced. Besides the [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] area of the south, there are significant mud {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}} in the northern part of the island, around {{ill|Beppu|en|Beppu|WD=Q273880|lt=Beppu}}. The springs are the site of occurrence of certain {{ill|Extremophile|en|Extremophile|WD=Q206912|lt=Extremophile}} {{ill|Microorganism|en|Microorganism|WD=Q39833|lt=Microorganism}}s, which are capable of surviving in extremely hot environments.C. Michael Hogan. 2010. [http://www.eoearth.org/article/Extremophile?topic=49540 ''Extremophile'']. eds. E. Monosson and C. Cleveland. Encyclopedia of Earth. National Council for Science and the Environment, Washington DC There are two World Natural Heritage sites in Kyushu: {{ill|Yakushima|en|Yakushima|WD=Q242176|lt=Yakushima}} (registered in 1993) and {{ill|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|en|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|WD=Q11444847|lt=Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island}} (registered in 2021).{{Cite web|title=日本の世界遺産一覧 |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/|website=文化庁|language=ja| access-date=2023-05-22}} ==Economy == {{main|Economy of Japan}} [[Image:M-V with ASTRO-E2 on launch pad.jpeg|thumb|M-V rocket launch rehearsal at USC]] Kyushu's economy accounts for about 10% of Japan's total, and with a GDP equivalent to that of Iran, the 26th largest country in the world, it is the fourth largest economic zone after the three major metropolitan areas of {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}, and {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|WD=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}}.{{Cite web|title=potential of Kyushu |url=https://www.fukuoka-fg.com/vision/03.html|website=Fukuoka financial group|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-16}} Kyushu's economy has a well-balanced industrial structure, ranging from primary industries such as agriculture, to secondary industries such as manufacturing, and tertiary industries such as retail, services, and tourism. Agricultural output in the region amounts to 1.8 trillion yen (20% share of the national total), and the region is a major domestic production center for the [[:en:Automobile|Automobile]] and {{ill|Semiconductor|en|Semiconductor|WD=Q11456|lt=Semiconductor}} industries. Kyushu also has a thriving healthcare industry, including medical and nursing care, and numerous research and manufacturing facilities in the fields of {{ill|Hydrogen|en|Hydrogen|WD=Q556|lt=Hydrogen}}, {{ill|Solar power|en|Solar power|WD=Q1483757|lt=Solar power}}, and other renewable energies. Furthermore, [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], [[:en:Kitakyushu City|Kitakyushu City]] and {{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa Prefecture}} have been designated as [[National Strategic Special Zones]], which are expected to have an economic ripple effect on the entire Kyushu region through the creation of innovation in industry and the promotion of new entrepreneurship and start-ups. Kyushu is a region with strong economic ties to Asia. For example, Asia accounted for 420 (77.9%) of the 539 overseas expansion cases of Kyushu-Yamaguchi companies from 2010 to 2019, and Asia accounted for 61.1% of Kyushu-Yamaguchi's total exports in 2019, 7.4 percentage points higher than the nation as a whole. As the logistics node between Japan and Asia, the ports of Hakata and Kitakyushu handle a large number of international containers. In addition, the number of cruise ship calls in 2019 was 772, with Kyushu accounting for 26.9% of the nation's total.{{Cite web|title=はじめての九州経済 |url=https://www.kerc.or.jp/economy/gaikan/|website=Kyushu economic research center|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-22}} Kyushu is noted for various types of {{ill|Porcelain|en|Porcelain|WD=Q130693|lt=Porcelain}}, including Arita, Imari, Satsuma, and Karatsu. {{ill|Heavy industry|en|Heavy industry|WD=Q622662|lt=Heavy industry}} is concentrated in the north around Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, Nagasaki, and Oita and includes chemicals, automobiles, semiconductors, metal processing, shipbuilding, etc.{{Cite web|title=JAPAN PRODUCTS: Business Directory of Japanese Companies.|url=http://japan-product.com/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-28}} The island of {{ill|Tanegashima|en|Tanegashima|WD=Q696228|lt=Tanegashima}} hosts the {{ill|Tanegashima Space Center|en|Tanegashima Space Center|WD=Q742683|lt=Tanegashima Space Center}}, which is the largest rocket-launch complex in Japan. ==Transportation== Kyushu is linked to the larger island of [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|WD=Q15972411|lt=Kanmon Railway Tunnel}},{{Cite web|title=Kanmon Tunnel {{!}} Description, History, Construction, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kanmon-Tunnel|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}} which carries the non-{{ill|Shinkansen|en|Shinkansen|WD=Q164338|lt=Shinkansen}} trains of the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}}, and the newer {{ill|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|en|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|WD=Q8016189|lt=Shin-Kanmon Tunnel}} carrying the {{ill|San'yō Shinkansen|en|San'yō Shinkansen|WD=Q615964|lt=San'yō Shinkansen}}. Railways on the island are operated by the Kyushu Railway Company and {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|WD=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}}, as well as a variety of smaller companies such as {{ill|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|en|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|WD=Q642407|lt=Amagi Railway}}{{Cite web|title=Railways in Kyushu|url=https://www.sinfin.net/railways/world/japan/kyushu.html|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.sinfin.net}} and {{ill|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|en|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|WD=Q869251|lt=Nishitetsu Railway}}.{{Cite web|title=Railways in Northern Kyushu|url=http://www.japaneserailwaysociety.com/jrs/members/oliver/kyushu/kyushu.htm|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.japaneserailwaysociety.com}} {{ill|Kyushu Shinkansen|en|Kyushu Shinkansen|WD=Q11370254|lt=Kyushu Shinkansen}} trains operate between major cities on the island,{{Cite web|title=Getting Around {{!}} Kyushu Tourism Promotion Organization|url=https://www.visit-kyushu.com/en/plan-your-trip/getting-around/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.visit-kyushu.com|language=en}} such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kagoshima|en|Kagoshima|WD=Q15674|lt=Kagoshima}},{{Cite web|title=Kyushu Shinkansen|url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=[[Japan Visitor]] |archive-date=2021-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020112050/https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen}} with an additional route between {{STN|Takeo-Onsen}} and {{ill|Nagasaki|en|Nagasaki|WD=Q38234|lt=Nagasaki}} which is in operation since September 2022.{{Cite web|date=2020-07-10|title=Fukuoka to Nagasaki: How to go from Fukuoka to Nagasaki? {{!}} Japan-Rail-Pass|url=https://www.japan-rail-pass.com/node/4326|access-date=2022-04-21|website=Japan Rail Pass {{!}} Japan Rail Pass |language=en}} Kyushu is also known for its scenic train services, such as the Limited Express Yufuin no Mori and Limited Express Kawasemi Yamasemi. The {{ill|Kanmon Bridge|en|Kanmon Bridge|WD=Q1196470|lt=Kanmon Bridge}} and {{ill|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|WD=Q15972446|lt=Kanmon Roadway Tunnel}} also connect the island with Honshu, allowing for vehicular transport between the two.{{Cite web|last=MATCHA |title=Walk From Honshu To Kyushu! 4 Ways To Cross Between The Two Islands|url=https://matcha-jp.com/en/1737|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MATCHA - JAPAN TRAVEL WEB MAGAZINE |language=en}} The {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|en|Kyushu Expressway|WD=Q1060803|lt=Kyushu Expressway}} spans the length of the island, linking the {{ill|Higashikyushu Expressway|en|Higashikyushu Expressway|WD=Q2648028|lt=Higashikyushu Expressway}} and Ibusuki Skyline, connecting major cities such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kumamoto|en|Kumamoto|WD=Q199889|lt=Kumamoto}} along the way.{{Cite web |title=Kyushu Expy · Japan |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Kyushu+Expy,+Japan/@32.7319959,130.7735981,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x3540f3427949e6d9:0x60891c7c25263c3!8m2!3d32.7319914!4d130.7757868 |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=Kyushu Expy · Japan |language=en}} There are also many quiet country roads, including popular tourist routes such as the {{ill|Nichinan, Miyazaki|en|Nichinan, Miyazaki|WD=Q860669|lt=Nichinan}} coast road and the Aso Panorama Line in {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|Kumamoto Prefecture|WD=Q130308|lt=Kumamoto Prefecture}}. Bus services are available and cover 2,400 routes within Kyushu's cities, connecting many other destinations. Several passenger and car ferry services connect both northern and southern Kyushu with main port cities on the main island of Honshu (Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo) and [[Shikoku]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2355.html|title = Domestic Ferries| date=May 2022 }} ==Education== [[File:Kyushumap-en.png|320px|thumb|Map of Kyushu region with prefectures]] [[File:JMSDF major (2005). "Kyūshū" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|''Japan Encyclopedia'', p. 588|page=588}} In the past, it has been known as {{nihongo3|"Nine Countries"|九国|Kyūkoku}}, {{nihongo3|"West of the Pacified Area"|鎮西|Chinzei}} and {{nihongo3|"Island of Tsukushi"|{{lang|ja|筑紫島}}|Tsukushi-no-shima}}. The historical regional name {{nihongo|{{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}}|{{lang|ja|西海道}}||{{lit}} West Sea [[:en:Circuit (country subdivision)|Circuit]]}} referred to Kyushu and its surrounding islands. Kyushu has a land area of {{convert|36782|km2|sqmi}} and a population of 14,311,224 in 2018. In the 8th-century {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|WD=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} reforms, {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} was established as a special administrative term for the region.Nussbaum, "Dazaifu" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|p. 150|page=150}}; [http://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4850.html Dazaifu] ==Geography== [[File:Kyushu-Japan-ISS-Space.png|thumb|250px|Kyushu from the {{ill|International Space Station|en|International Space Station|WD=Q25271|lt=International Space Station}}]] [[File:Geofeatures_map_of_Kyushu_Japan_ja.svg|thumb|315x315px|Geofeatures map of Kyushu]] The island is mountainous, and Japan's most active volcano, {{ill|Mount Aso|en|Mount Aso|WD=Q733710|lt=Mount Aso}} at {{convert|1591|m}}, is on Kyushu. There are many other signs of tectonic activity, including numerous areas of {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}}s. The most famous of these are in [[:en:Beppu, Ōita|Beppu]], on the east shore, and around Mt. Aso in central Kyushu. The island is separated from [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Straits|en|Kanmon Straits|WD=Q494894|lt=Kanmon Straits}}. Being the nearest island to the {{ill|Asia|en|Asia|WD=Q48|lt=Asian continent}},Nussbaum, Louis-Frédéric and Käthe Roth (2005). [https://books.google.com/books?id=p2QnPijAEmEC ''Japan Encyclopedia'']. Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-674-01753-5}}. {{OCLC|58053128}}. historically it is the gateway to Japan.{{Cite book |title=Kyushu, gateway to Japan : a concise history |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=157 |oclc=754792858}} The total area is {{convert|36,782.37|km²|sqmi|abbr=on}} which makes it the 37th {{ill|en:List of islands by area|en|en:List of islands by area|WD=Q104176|lt=largest island}} in the world.{{Cite web |date=2016-10-01 |url=http://www.gsi.go.jp/KOKUJYOHO/MENCHO/201610/f3_shima.pdf |title=平成28th year 全国都道府県市区町村別面積調 島面積 |publisher=[[国土地理院]] |accessdate=2017-02-27}} It's slightly larger than {{ill|Geography of Taiwan|en|Geography of Taiwan|WD=Q22528|lt=Taiwan}} island {{convert|35,808|km2|sqmi|abbr=on}}.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thoughtco.com/islands-of-japan-1435071|title=Discover the Geography of the 4 Main Islands of Japan |work=ThoughtCo |access-date=2018-09-26}} The highest elevation is {{convert|1791|m|0|abbr=off|comma=5|sp=us}} on [[Mount Kujū]].{{cite web |url=http://www.peaklist.org/WWlists/ultras/japan.html |title=Japan Ultra-Prominences |publisher=Peaklist.org |accessdate=2015-01-01}} The name ''Kyūshū'' comes from the nine ancient provinces of {{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}} situated on the island: {{ill|Chikuzen Province|en|Chikuzen Province|WD=Q1047664|lt=Chikuzen}}, {{ill|Chikugo Province|en|Chikugo Province|WD=Q864159|lt=Chikugo}}, {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen}}, {{ill|Higo Province|en|Higo Province|WD=Q259705|lt=Higo}}, {{ill|Buzen Province|en|Buzen Province|WD=Q1047134|lt=Buzen}}, {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|WD=Q864148|lt=Bungo}}, {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|WD=Q513737|lt=Hyūga}}, {{ill|Ōsumi Province|en|Ōsumi Province|WD=Q981002|lt=Osumi}}, and {{ill|Satsuma Province|en|Satsuma Kyushu's population is concentrated along the northwest, in the cities of {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kitakyushu|en|Kitakyushu|WD=Q188806|lt=Kitakyushu}}, with population corridors stretching southwest into {{ill|Sasebo|en|Sasebo|WD=Q328000|lt=Sasebo}} and {{ill|Nagasaki|en|Nagasaki|WD=Q38234|lt=Nagasaki}} and south into {{ill|Kumamoto|en|Kumamoto|WD=Q199889|lt=Kumamoto}} and {{ill|Kagoshima|en|Kagoshima|WD=Q15674|lt=Kagoshima}}. Except for {{ill|Ōita (city)|en|Ōita (city)|WD=Q199609|lt=Oita}} and {{ill|Miyazaki (city)|en|Miyazaki (city)|WD=Q204308|lt=Miyazaki}}, the eastern seaboard shows a general {{ill|Demographics of Japan|en|Demographics of Japan|WD=Q1124220|lt=decline in population}}. Politically, Kyushu is described as a stronghold of the {{ill|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|en|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|WD=Q232595|lt=Liberal Democratic Party}}.{{cite news|title=Japanese voters want a plan to handle a declining population|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21730003-election-campaign-disappointing-them-japanese-voters-want-plan-handle-declining|newspaper={{ill|The Economist|en|The Economist|WD=Q180089|lt=The Economist}}|date=5 October 2017}} Per Japanese census data,{{Cite web|url=https://www.citypopulation.de/en/japan/cities/fukuoka/|title=Fukuoka (Japan): Prefecture, Major Cities & Towns - Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |website=www.citypopulation.de}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.demographia.com/db-japanpref.htm|title=Japan Prefectures Population from 1920 and Area |website=www.demographia.com}} the Kyushu region's population with {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|en|Ryukyu Islands|WD=Q6897416|lt=Ryukyu Islands}} ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}} Prefectures) has experienced a large population decline since around 2000. However, the population decline in total is mild because of the relatively high birth rate of {{ill|Ryukyuans|en|Ryukyuans|WD=Q1208167|lt=Ryukyuans}} both within the Ryukyuan lands ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}}) and throughout the Kyushu region. In addition, the other prefectures in Kyushu also have exceptionally high [[Total fertility rate#Japan|TFR]]s compared to the rest of Japan.[https://www8.cao.go.jp/shoushi/shoushika/research/cyousa23/kankyo/pdf/5.pdf 「都市と地方における子育て環境の違いから得られた知見」]{{Cite web|url=https://www.mhlw.go.jp/toukei/saikin/hw/jinkou/geppo/nengai20/dl/h9.pdf|title=令和２年(2020)人口動態統計月報年計（概数）の概況}} The Ryukyuans are an {{ill|Indigenous peoples|en|Indigenous have a [[:en:Subtropical climate|Subtropical climate]], particularly {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture}}. Major agricultural products are {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}}, {{ill|Tea|en|Tea|WD=Q6097|lt=Tea}}, {{ill|Tobacco|en|Tobacco|WD=Q1566|lt=Tobacco}}, {{ill|Sweet potato|en|Sweet potato|WD=Q37937|lt=Sweet potato}}es, and [[:en:Soy|Soy]]; also, {{ill|Silk|en|Silk|WD=Q37681|lt=Silk}} is widely produced. Besides the [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] area of the south, there are significant mud {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}} in the northern part of the island, around {{ill|Beppu|en|Beppu|WD=Q273880|lt=Beppu}}. The springs are the site of occurrence of certain {{ill|Extremophile|en|Extremophile|WD=Q206912|lt=Extremophile}} {{ill|Microorganism|en|Microorganism|WD=Q39833|lt=Microorganism}}s, which are capable of surviving in extremely hot environments.C. Michael Hogan. 2010. [http://www.eoearth.org/article/Extremophile?topic=49540 ''Extremophile'']. eds. E. Monosson and C. Cleveland. Encyclopedia of Earth. National Council for Science and the Environment, Washington DC There are two World Natural Heritage sites in Kyushu: {{ill|Yakushima|en|Yakushima|WD=Q242176|lt=Yakushima}} (registered in 1993) and {{ill|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|en|Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island|WD=Q11444847|lt=Amami-Ōshima Island, Tokunoshima Island, northern part of Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island}} (registered in 2021).{{Cite web|title=日本の世界遺産一覧 |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/|website=文化庁|language=ja| access-date=2023-05-22}} ==Economy == {{main|Economy of Japan}} [[Image:M-V with ASTRO-E2 on launch pad.jpeg|thumb|M-V rocket launch rehearsal at USC]] Kyushu's economy accounts for about 10% of Japan's total, and with a GDP equivalent to that of Iran, the 26th largest country in the world, it is the fourth largest economic zone after the three major metropolitan areas of {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka}}, and {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|WD=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}}.{{Cite web|title=potential of Kyushu |url=https://www.fukuoka-fg.com/vision/03.html|website=Fukuoka financial group|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-16}} Kyushu's economy has a well-balanced industrial structure, ranging from primary industries such as agriculture, to secondary industries such as manufacturing, and tertiary industries such as retail, services, and tourism. Agricultural output in the region amounts to 1.8 trillion yen (20% share of the national total), and the region is a major domestic production center for the [[:en:Automobile|Automobile]] and {{ill|Semiconductor|en|Semiconductor|WD=Q11456|lt=Semiconductor}} industries. Kyushu also has a thriving healthcare industry, including medical and nursing care, and numerous research and manufacturing facilities in the fields of {{ill|Hydrogen|en|Hydrogen|WD=Q556|lt=Hydrogen}}, {{ill|Solar power|en|Solar power|WD=Q1483757|lt=Solar power}}, and other renewable energies. Furthermore, [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], [[:en:Kitakyushu City|Kitakyushu City]] and {{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa Prefecture}} have been designated as [[National Strategic Special Zones]], which are expected to have an economic ripple effect on the entire Kyushu region through the creation of innovation in industry and the promotion of new entrepreneurship and start-ups. Kyushu is a region with strong economic ties to Asia. For example, Asia accounted for 420 (77.9%) of the 539 overseas expansion cases of Kyushu-Yamaguchi companies from 2010 to 2019, and Asia accounted for 61.1% of Kyushu-Yamaguchi's total exports in 2019, 7.4 percentage points higher than the nation as a whole. As the logistics node between Japan and Asia, the ports of Hakata and Kitakyushu handle a large number of international containers. In addition, the number of cruise ship calls in 2019 was 772, with Kyushu accounting for 26.9% of the nation's total.{{Cite web|title=はじめての九州経済 |url=https://www.kerc.or.jp/economy/gaikan/|website=Kyushu economic research center|language=ja|access-date=2023-05-22}} Kyushu is noted for various types of {{ill|Porcelain|en|Porcelain|WD=Q130693|lt=Porcelain}}, including Arita, Imari, Satsuma, and Karatsu. {{ill|Heavy industry|en|Heavy industry|WD=Q622662|lt=Heavy industry}} is concentrated in the north around Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, Nagasaki, and Oita and includes chemicals, automobiles, semiconductors, metal processing, shipbuilding, etc.{{Cite web|title=JAPAN PRODUCTS: Business Directory of Japanese Companies.|url=http://japan-product.com/|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-28}} The island of {{ill|Tanegashima|en|Tanegashima|WD=Q696228|lt=Tanegashima}} hosts the {{ill|Tanegashima Space Center|en|Tanegashima Space Center|WD=Q742683|lt=Tanegashima Space Center}}, which is the largest rocket-launch complex in Japan. ==Transportation== Kyushu is linked to the larger island of [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Railway Tunnel|WD=Q15972411|lt=Kanmon Railway Tunnel}},{{Cite web|title=Kanmon Tunnel {{!}} Description, History, Construction, & Facts |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kanmon-Tunnel|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}} which carries the non-{{ill|Shinkansen|en|Shinkansen|WD=Q164338|lt=Shinkansen}} trains of the {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}}, and the newer {{ill|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|en|Shin-Kanmon Tunnel|WD=Q8016189|lt=Shin-Kanmon Tunnel}} carrying the {{ill|San'yō Shinkansen|en|San'yō Shinkansen|WD=Q615964|lt=San'yō Shinkansen}}. Railways on the island are operated by the Kyushu Railway Company and {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|WD=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}}, as well as a variety of smaller companies such as {{ill|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|en|Amagi Railway Amagi Line|WD=Q642407|lt=Amagi Railway}}{{Cite web|title=Railways in Kyushu|url=https://www.sinfin.net/railways/world/japan/kyushu.html|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.sinfin.net}} and {{ill|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|en|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|WD=Q869251|lt=Nishitetsu Railway}}.{{Cite web|title=Railways in Northern Kyushu|url=http://www.japaneserailwaysociety.com/jrs/members/oliver/kyushu/kyushu.htm|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.japaneserailwaysociety.com}} {{ill|Kyushu Shinkansen|en|Kyushu Shinkansen|WD=Q11370254|lt=Kyushu Shinkansen}} trains operate between major cities on the island,{{Cite web|title=Getting Around {{!}} Kyushu Tourism Promotion Organization|url=https://www.visit-kyushu.com/en/plan-your-trip/getting-around/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.visit-kyushu.com|language=en}} such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kagoshima|en|Kagoshima|WD=Q15674|lt=Kagoshima}},{{Cite web|title=Kyushu Shinkansen|url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-20|website=[[Japan Visitor]] |archive-date=2021-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020112050/https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-travel/kyushu-shinkansen}} with an additional route between {{STN|Takeo-Onsen}} and {{ill|Nagasaki|en|Nagasaki|WD=Q38234|lt=Nagasaki}} which is in operation since September 2022.{{Cite web|date=2020-07-10|title=Fukuoka to Nagasaki: How to go from Fukuoka to Nagasaki? {{!}} Japan-Rail-Pass|url=https://www.japan-rail-pass.com/node/4326|access-date=2022-04-21|website=Japan Rail Pass {{!}} Japan Rail Pass |language=en}} Kyushu is also known for its scenic train services, such as the Limited Express Yufuin no Mori and Limited Express Kawasemi Yamasemi. The {{ill|Kanmon Bridge|en|Kanmon Bridge|WD=Q1196470|lt=Kanmon Bridge}} and {{ill|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|en|Kanmon Roadway Tunnel|WD=Q15972446|lt=Kanmon Roadway Tunnel}} also connect the island with Honshu, allowing for vehicular transport between the two.{{Cite web|last=MATCHA |title=Walk From Honshu To Kyushu! 4 Ways To Cross Between The Two Islands|url=https://matcha-jp.com/en/1737|access-date=2021-10-20|website=MATCHA - JAPAN TRAVEL WEB MAGAZINE |language=en}} The {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|en|Kyushu Expressway|WD=Q1060803|lt=Kyushu Expressway}} spans the length of the island, linking the {{ill|Higashikyushu Expressway|en|Higashikyushu Expressway|WD=Q2648028|lt=Higashikyushu Expressway}} and Ibusuki Skyline, connecting major cities such as {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kumamoto|en|Kumamoto|WD=Q199889|lt=Kumamoto}} along the way.{{Cite web |title=Kyushu Expy · Japan |url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/Kyushu+Expy,+Japan/@32.7319959,130.7735981,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x3540f3427949e6d9:0x60891c7c25263c3!8m2!3d32.7319914!4d130.7757868 |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=Kyushu Expy · Japan |language=en}} There are also many quiet country roads, including popular tourist routes such as the {{ill|Nichinan, Miyazaki|en|Nichinan, Miyazaki|WD=Q860669|lt=Nichinan}} coast road and the Aso Panorama Line in {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|Kumamoto Prefecture|WD=Q130308|lt=Kumamoto Prefecture}}. Bus services are available and cover 2,400 routes within Kyushu's cities, connecting many other destinations. Several passenger and car ferry services connect both northern and southern Kyushu with main port cities on the main island of Honshu (Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo) and [[Shikoku]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2355.html|title = Domestic Ferries| date=May 2022 }} ==Education== [[File:Kyushumap-en.png|320px|thumb|Map of Kyushu region with prefectures]] [[File:JMSDF major (2005). "Kyūshū" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|''Japan Encyclopedia'', p. 588|page=588}} In the past, it has been known as {{nihongo3|"Nine Countries"|九国|Kyūkoku}}, {{nihongo3|"West of the Pacified Area"|鎮西|Chinzei}} and {{nihongo3|"Island of Tsukushi"|{{lang|ja|筑紫島}}|Tsukushi-no-shima}}. The historical regional name {{nihongo|{{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}}|{{lang|ja|西海道}}||{{lit}} West Sea [[:en:Circuit (country subdivision)|Circuit]]}} referred to Kyushu and its surrounding islands. Kyushu has a land area of {{convert|36782|km2|sqmi}} and a population of 14,311,224 in 2018. In the 8th-century {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|WD=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} reforms, {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} was established as a special administrative term for the region.Nussbaum, "Dazaifu" in {{Google books|p2QnPijAEmEC|p. 150|page=150}}; [http://www.japan-guide.com/e/e4850.html Dazaifu] ==Geography== [[File:Kyushu-Japan-ISS-Space.png|thumb|250px|Kyushu from the {{ill|International Space Station|en|International Space Station|WD=Q25271|lt=International Space Station}}]] [[File:Geofeatures_map_of_Kyushu_Japan_ja.svg|thumb|315x315px|Geofeatures map of Kyushu]] The island is mountainous, and Japan's most active volcano, {{ill|Mount Aso|en|Mount Aso|WD=Q733710|lt=Mount Aso}} at {{convert|1591|m}}, is on Kyushu. There are many other signs of tectonic activity, including numerous areas of {{ill|Hot spring|en|Hot spring|WD=Q177380|lt=Hot spring}}s. The most famous of these are in [[:en:Beppu, Ōita|Beppu]], on the east shore, and around Mt. Aso in central Kyushu. The island is separated from [[Honshu]] by the {{ill|Kanmon Straits|en|Kanmon Straits|WD=Q494894|lt=Kanmon Straits}}. Being the nearest island to the {{ill|Asia|en|Asia|WD=Q48|lt=Asian continent}},Nussbaum, Louis-Frédéric and Käthe Roth (2005). [https://books.google.com/books?id=p2QnPijAEmEC ''Japan Encyclopedia'']. Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press. {{ISBN|978-0-674-01753-5}}. {{OCLC|58053128}}. historically it is the gateway to Japan.{{Cite book |title=Kyushu, gateway to Japan : a concise history |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=157 |oclc=754792858}} The total area is {{convert|36,782.37|km²|sqmi|abbr=on}} which makes it the 37th {{ill|en:List of islands by area|en|en:List of islands by area|WD=Q104176|lt=largest island}} in the world.{{Cite web |date=2016-10-01 |url=http://www.gsi.go.jp/KOKUJYOHO/MENCHO/201610/f3_shima.pdf |title=平成28th year 全国都道府県市区町村別面積調 島面積 |publisher=[[国土地理院]] |accessdate=2017-02-27}} It's slightly larger than {{ill|Geography of Taiwan|en|Geography of Taiwan|WD=Q22528|lt=Taiwan}} island {{convert|35,808|km2|sqmi|abbr=on}}.{{Cite news|url=https://www.thoughtco.com/islands-of-japan-1435071|title=Discover the Geography of the 4 Main Islands of Japan |work=ThoughtCo |access-date=2018-09-26}} The highest elevation is {{convert|1791|m|0|abbr=off|comma=5|sp=us}} on [[Mount Kujū]].{{cite web |url=http://www.peaklist.org/WWlists/ultras/japan.html |title=Japan Ultra-Prominences |publisher=Peaklist.org |accessdate=2015-01-01}} The name ''Kyūshū'' comes from the nine ancient provinces of {{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|WD=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō}} situated on the island: {{ill|Chikuzen Province|en|Chikuzen Province|WD=Q1047664|lt=Chikuzen}}, {{ill|Chikugo Province|en|Chikugo Province|WD=Q864159|lt=Chikugo}}, {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen}}, {{ill|Higo Province|en|Higo Province|WD=Q259705|lt=Higo}}, {{ill|Buzen Province|en|Buzen Province|WD=Q1047134|lt=Buzen}}, {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|WD=Q864148|lt=Bungo}}, {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|WD=Q513737|lt=Hyūga}}, {{ill|Ōsumi Province|en|Ōsumi Province|WD=Q981002|lt=Osumi}}, and {{ill|Satsuma Province|en|Satsuma Province|WD=Q667475|lt=Satsuma}}.{{Cite book|title=Kyushu, Gateway to Japan: A Concise History |first=Andrew |last=Cobbing |date=2009 |publisher=Global Oriental |isbn=9789004213128 |pages=3 |oclc=754792858}} Today's {{nihongo|Kyushu Region|{{lang|ja|九州地方}}|Kyūshū-chihō}} is a politically defined region that consists of the seven {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|WD=Q50337|lt=prefecture}}s on the island of Kyushu (which also includes the former {{ill|Tsushima Province|en|Tsushima Province|WD=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima}} and {{ill|Iki Province|en|Iki Province|WD=Q1052938|lt=Iki}} as part of Nagasaki), plus {{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa Prefecture}} to the south: * {{ill|Northern Kyushu|en|Northern Kyushu|WD=Q397703|lt=Northern Kyushu}} ** {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} ** {{ill|Kumamoto Prefecture|en|Kumamoto Prefecture|WD=Q130308|lt=Kumamoto Prefecture}} ** {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|en|Nagasaki Prefecture|WD=Q169376|lt=Nagasaki Prefecture}} ** {{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|WD=Q133924|lt=Ōita Prefecture}} ** {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} * {{ill|Southern Kyushu|en|Southern Kyushu|WD=Q8017707|lt=Southern Kyushu}} ** {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima Prefecture}} ** {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}} *{{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} ** {{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa Prefecture}} ==Population== Kyushu has 10.3{{nbsp}}percent of the population of Japan.{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=90C4DgAAQBAJ&pg=PA16| page=16| title=The Philippine Archipelago |first=Yves |last=Boquet |publisher=Springer |year= 2017|isbn= 9783319519265}} Most of Kyushu's population is concentrated along the northwest, in the cities of {{ill|Fukuoka|en|Fukuoka|WD=Q26600|lt=Fukuoka}} and {{ill|Kitakyushu|en|Kitakyushu|WD=Q188806|lt=Kitakyushu}}, with population corridors stretching southwest into {{ill|Sasebo|en|Sasebo|WD=Q328000|lt=Sasebo}} and {{ill|Nagasaki|en|Nagasaki|WD=Q38234|lt=Nagasaki}} and south into {{ill|Kumamoto|en|Kumamoto|WD=Q199889|lt=Kumamoto}} and {{ill|Kagoshima|en|Kagoshima|WD=Q15674|lt=Kagoshima}}. Except for {{ill|Ōita (city)|en|Ōita (city)|WD=Q199609|lt=Oita}} and {{ill|Miyazaki (city)|en|Miyazaki (city)|WD=Q204308|lt=Miyazaki}}, the eastern seaboard shows a general {{ill|Demographics of Japan|en|Demographics of Japan|WD=Q1124220|lt=decline in population}}. Politically, Kyushu is described as a stronghold of the {{ill|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|en|Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|WD=Q232595|lt=Liberal Democratic Party}}.{{cite news|title=Japanese voters want a plan to handle a declining population|url=https://www.economist.com/news/asia/21730003-election-campaign-disappointing-them-japanese-voters-want-plan-handle-declining|newspaper={{ill|The Economist|en|The Economist|WD=Q180089|lt=The Economist}}|date=5 October 2017}} Per Japanese census data,{{Cite web|url=https://www.citypopulation.de/en/japan/cities/fukuoka/|title=Fukuoka (Japan): Prefecture, Major Cities & Towns - Population Statistics, Maps, Charts, Weather and Web Information |website=www.citypopulation.de}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.demographia.com/db-japanpref.htm|title=Japan Prefectures Population from 1920 and Area |website=www.demographia.com}} the Kyushu region's population with {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|en|Ryukyu Islands|WD=Q6897416|lt=Ryukyu Islands}} ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}} Prefectures) has experienced a large population decline since around 2000. However, the population decline in total is mild because of the relatively high birth rate of {{ill|Ryukyuans|en|Ryukyuans|WD=Q1208167|lt=Ryukyuans}} both within the Ryukyuan lands ({{ill|Okinawa Prefecture|en|Okinawa Prefecture|WD=Q766445|lt=Okinawa}} and {{ill|Kagoshima Prefecture|en|Kagoshima Prefecture|WD=Q15701|lt=Kagoshima}}) and throughout the Kyushu region. In addition, the other prefectures in Kyushu also have exceptionally high [[Total fertility rate#Japan|TFR]]s compared to the rest of Japan.[https://www8.cao.go.jp/shoushi/shoushika/research/cyousa23/kankyo/pdf/5.pdf 「都市と地方における子育て環境の違いから得られた知見」]{{Cite web|url=https://www.mhlw.go.jp/toukei/saikin/hw/jinkou/geppo/nengai20/dl/h9.pdf|title=令和２年(2020)人口動態統計月報年計（概数）の概況}} The Ryukyuans are an {{ill|Indigenous peoples|en|Indigenous peoples|WD=Q103817|lt=indigenous}} minority group in Japan. {| |+'''Historical populations''' |valign="top"|'''Including {{ill|Ryukyu Islands|en|Ryukyu Islands|WD=Q6897416|lt=Ryukyu Islands}}''' 14,518,000 | 2000 | 14,763,781 | 2010 | 14,596,783 | 2018 | 14,311,224 |align = none | footnote = Includes Okinawa and Kagoshima prefecture populations. }} |'''Excluding Ryukyu Islands''' {{Historical
